references.observation: Aimlabs groups its general fundamentals around flicking, target switching and tracking, with smaller task variations under each category.
references.principle: Keep the core aiming skills separate so a short session can isolate a weakness instead of mixing every input into one score.
references.application: Flickyard exposes distinct Flick, Track and Switch drills, then combines them in a fixed three-stage 90-second circuit.
references.avoid: Do not copy Aimlabs branding, target art, screen layout or named scenario content.

references.observation: KovaaK's workshop organizes a large community scenario library, including separate tracking, clicking and switching scenarios.
references.principle: A training task should have a clear input contract and adjustable parameters rather than one universal difficulty curve.
references.application: Each Flickyard mode has its own scoring rule, duration and target behavior, with a separate difficulty selector.
references.avoid: Do not reproduce the workshop catalogue, community marketplace or its weapon-oriented presentation.

references.observation: 3D Aim Trainer offers a browser entry point alongside its downloadable desktop experience and describes drills for mouse accuracy, flicking and tracking.
references.principle: A browser trainer should reach its first useful exercise quickly and retain meaningful local feedback after a session.
references.application: Flickyard launches directly into a ready range, works without a network connection and stores personal bests on the device.
references.avoid: Do not imitate its game-specific 3D scenes, player leaderboard claims or external account flow.

concepts.medium: A hand-authored 2D Canvas range with layered steel rails, ceramic target faces, brass fasteners and small impact fragments.
concepts.composition: A wide open horizontal playfield occupies most of the screen, with one narrow drill rail and a separate results ledger.
concepts.interaction: Mouse movement directly controls the reticle; left click fires, while a dedicated tracking task scores continuous on-target time.
concepts.motion: Targets slide on rails, make small readable direction corrections and rotate with inertia when struck.
concepts.rationale: This direction keeps the mouse path honest, renders sharply in the browser and gives every hit a tactile mechanical consequence.

concepts.medium: A precise SVG calibration instrument with etched glass rings, a movable optical iris and printed measurement scales.
concepts.composition: One centered instrument fills a narrow portrait workbench, with a compact row of calibration controls beneath it.
concepts.interaction: The player adjusts a lens aperture and dials sensitivity before running a static alignment test.
concepts.motion: Dials rotate slowly and the lens closes with a damped mechanical stop, emphasizing calibration rather than target contact.
concepts.rationale: It is useful for mouse setup but does not create enough repeated target acquisition to sustain an aim-training loop.

concepts.medium: A WebGL 3D gallery of floating ceramic spheres, volumetric spotlights and orbital target rigs.
concepts.composition: A circular three-dimensional arena surrounds a central camera, with a floating bottom HUD and radial mode selector.
concepts.interaction: The player uses pointer lock to turn freely in three dimensions and fires at targets moving in depth.
concepts.motion: Targets orbit, drift toward and away from the camera, and break into volumetric shards after impact.
concepts.rationale: The 3D camera adds depth and spectacle but makes browser performance and consistent mouse benchmarking harder to control.

selection.reason: A 2D horizontal range gives predictable mouse coordinates, high refresh responsiveness and a distinct physical identity without external assets or a heavy renderer.

rejected.reason: A calibration instrument is a useful setup utility, but its dial interaction does not provide repeated flicking, tracking and switching practice.
A 3D orbital arena introduces camera acceleration and depth perception variables that weaken repeatable mouse-skill measurement in a browser.

tools.reason: Native Canvas 2D is available in the quick runtime and supports a high-frequency pointer-driven target field without a remote renderer.
Inline SVG produces a crisp app icon and small mechanical marks with no raster download or external font dependency.
Web Audio can synthesize the enamel and steel contact from filtered noise and short independent resonances after a user gesture.

assets.role: The target plates, rails, measurement marks, reticle, hit rings and impact fragments form the only focal visual system.
assets.acceptance: Targets remain distinguishable at 13–27 CSS pixels and the active target is identifiable without relying on color alone.
assets.integration: The range is drawn in CSS-pixel coordinates with a capped device-pixel ratio and is resized proportionally during an active session.
assets.provenance: Original Canvas paths and geometry authored for Flickyard; no borrowed sprites, branded marks or stock imagery.

assets.role: A concentric target plate intersects two steel rails and one rust-red crosshair axis.
assets.acceptance: The plate, rails and center remain readable at 48 pixels without text or a generic monogram.
assets.integration: The same SVG is used by the PWA manifest, browser favicon and app launcher.
assets.provenance: Original hand-authored SVG paths and circles using the app palette.

assets.role: A hit combines a sharp filtered enamel tick with a low plate resonance; a miss is a softer felt-backed knock.
assets.acceptance: Hit, miss, selection and finish remain distinguishable at ordinary speaker volume with no harsh transient peak.
assets.integration: A lazy AudioContext creates a bounded number of procedural voices and is muted by a persistent settings control.
assets.provenance: Original browser synthesis using generated noise buffers and short oscillators; no external samples.

risks: Pointer Lock may be denied or released by Escape; visible-cursor fallback and pause behavior must remain reliable.
The target field must keep accurate CSS-pixel coordinates across high-DPI displays and browser resizing.
The left rail and result ledger must not cover the active target field on narrow landscape and portrait screens.
Target speed and impact fragments must not create frame-time spikes during rapid repeated hits.
